2-10-63.1 Purposes and intents; organization; division of fire prevention; administration.
(a) Purposes and intents. It is the primary purpose of this article to provide for the reasonable and realistic protection of life and property from the hazards created by fire out of control, smoke, explosion, or panic created from a fear of fire out of control, smoke, or explosion. It is the basic intent of this article to accomplish its primary purpose:
(1) Through education efforts and programs designed to change high-risk attitudes and behaviors that are the root causes of most fires out of control;
(2) Through consultations and informational programs, develop in the citizens of and visitors to the City of Rome and Floyd County, an awareness of the provisions of this article, and other applicable laws, codes, and standards, and aid them to determine the options available to correct hazards, problems, or violations identified;
(3) By providing through this article reasonable, realistic, and practical safeguards against fire out of control and its related hazards; and
(4) As may be deemed necessary, initiate enforcement and legal proceedings as set forth in this article to gain compliance with the provisions of this article and the codes and standards adopted by this article.
This article is hereby declared to be remedial and shall be construed to secure the beneficial interests and purposes thereof, which are public safety, health, and general welfare, through safety to life and property from fire out of control, explosion and other hazards incident to the use and occupancy of buildings, structures, facilities, or premises located in Floyd County.
(b) Organization and programs. There is hereby created the division of fire prevention within the Rome/Floyd Fire Department for the purpose of implementing the provisions of this article. The division shall be under the direction and general supervision of the fire marshal. The fire marshal is the fire code official for the purposes of this article for Floyd County. The fire marshal is responsible to the fire chief for the administration, implementation, and enforcement of the provisions of this article and for the direction and supervision of the division. The division shall strive to improve the safety and lives and property from fire out of control and its associated hazards within Floyd County through programs of safety education, through consultations, and through the inspection of buildings, structures, facilities, and premises as often as deemed appropriate by the fire marshal and fire chief. As the fire chief and fire marshal deem appropriate, the division may develop and implement, in coordination and cooperation with other departments, agencies or organizations, public or private, a comprehensive program of community emergency education.
(c) Appointment of the fire marshal. The fire marshal shall be appointed by the fire chief based on an evaluation of the applicant's qualifications. The appointment shall continue until the fire marshal vacates the position or is removed for cause in accordance with the applicable policies and regulations of the City of Rome and Rome-Floyd Fire Department.
(d) Assistance to the fire marshal. The fire chief may detail or assign members of the Rome-Floyd Fire Department to the division of fire prevention to assist the fire marshal. Such members shall be under the direction and supervision of the fire marshal during their detail or assignment to the division. The fire chief, upon request of the fire marshal, may fill positions deemed necessary for carrying out the purposes and programs of the division, in accordance with the personnel policies and regulations of the City of Rome. The selections shall be open to members and nonmembers of the Rome-Floyd Fire Department. Employees assigned to fill positions with the division shall be under the direction and supervision of the fire marshal.
(e) Enforcement assistance. The chief of police, the building official or law enforcement officers of Floyd County shall render assistance to the fire chief or the fire marshal upon request in the implementation and enforcement of this article.
2-10-63.2 Applicability of this article and adopted codes and standards.
(a) Applicability. The provisions of this article, and the codes and standards adopted by this article, shall apply to all new and existing buildings, structures, premises, facilities and conditions within Floyd County; provided, however, existing situations or conditions not in strict compliance with this article or the codes and standards adopted by this article, and not in contravention with state law, rules or regulations, may be continued unless they are deemed by the fire marshal to constitute a distinct hazard to life or to property from fire out of control, smoke or explosion. The provisions of this article shall not apply to the interior of one-family or two-family dwellings or to premises upon which such dwellings are located or to the interior of any apartment dwelling unit, provided such dwellings or apartments are used strictly for residential purposes. This article and the codes and standards adopted by this article shall apply to such dwelling units whenever an activity coming under this article is conducted therein and/or which creates a hazard from fire out of control, smoke or explosion to life or to property.
(b) Existing and special historic buildings. The provisions of this article shall apply to existing buildings or structures in Floyd County as provided in this article. The provisions of this article shall apply to existing buildings or structures and special buildings or structures identified by the federal government, State of Georgia, Floyd County, Georgia, or by the City of Rome, Georgia, as historic buildings; provided, however, the provisions of this article shall be coordinated by the fire marshal with the applicable provisions of federal, state, and local laws or regulations, as applicable.
(c) Federal or state authority. The provisions of this article shall not be held to deprive any federal or state agency, or any applicable governing body having jurisdiction, of any power or authority which it had on the effective date of the adoption of this article or any remedy then existing for the enforcement of its orders, nor shall it deprive an individual or corporation of its legal rights as provided by law.
2-10-63.3 Administrative liability.
(a) Administrative liability. Any officer or employee of Floyd County empowered or authorized to administer or act under the provisions of this article or other applicable codes or standards in force in Floyd County or required by the State of Georgia, and acting for the county or state in the discharge of his or her duties, shall not be held liable personally, and he or she is hereby relieved from all personal liability from any damages that may accrue to any person or property as a result of any act required, implied or permitted in the discharge of his or her duties, or as required, implied or permitted by this article or other applicable codes in force in the county or adopted or required by the State of Georgia, or as a result of the omission of any action required or authorized by this article or other applicable codes in force by the county or adopted or required by the State of Georgia. Any suit instituted against any officer or employee of the Floyd County in connection with the implementation of the provisions of this Code or other applicable codes in force in Floyd County or adopted or required by the State of Georgia shall be defended by the legal representative of the Floyd County until such matter is settled.
(b) Liability. Floyd County shall not be liable for any damage to persons or property from any act or any failure to act in connection with any provision of this article or other applicable law, regulation or codes in force in the city or adopted or required by the State of Georgia.
(c) Permitting and inspection. The inspection, approval or permitting of any building or plan by any employee of the Division of Fire Prevention of the Fire Department of Floyd County, under the requirements of this article, shall not be construed in any court as a warranty of the physical condition of such building or the adequacy of such plan. Neither Floyd County nor any employee thereof shall be liable in tort for damages for any defect or hazardous or illegal condition or inadequacy in such building or plan, nor for any component of such building which may occur subsequent to such inspection, approval or permitting.
2-10-63.4 Conducting inspections; right of entry; related provisions.
(a) Inspections. The fire marshal is authorized to inspect, or cause to be inspected, as he or she deems appropriate or necessary based on fire experience in the county, on complaint, or on other applicable grounds, and as resources permit, buildings, structures, premises, and facilities coming within the scope of this article. The purpose of such inspections is to ascertain if any conditions exist which could be reasonably construed to cause a fire out of control or explosion, or that could contribute to the spread of a fire out of control or its byproducts, or to ascertain any significant nonconformance with the purposes, intents and other provisions of this article or any other applicable law, rule or regulation affecting safety to life and/or property from fire out of control, explosion or the hazards related to same. The fire marshal is authorized to apply other applicable laws and to cause to be corrected any conditions which could be reasonably construed to cause a fire out of control or explosion or that could contribute to the spread of a fire out of control, or any significant nonconformance with the purposes, intents or provisions of this article affecting safety to life and/or property from fire out of control, explosion or the hazards related to same.
(b) Right of entry to conduct inspections. The fire marshal or his or her authorized representatives may, to the extent permitted by law, have free access to and the right to enter at all reasonable times any building, structure, facility, or premises, except single-family or two-family dwellings, located within Floyd County, whether completed or under construction, for the purpose of conducting inspections and otherwise implementing the provisions of this article. Before entering any building, structure, facility, or premises not normally open to the public, except when a fire out of control or other emergency condition exists or has occurred, the fire marshal or his representatives shall obtain the consent of the occupant, owner, or person in charge at the time. Where consent to enter is refused, the fire marshal may seek an order or an administrative search warrant from the Magistrate Court of Floyd County, or if deemed appropriate, from the Superior Court of Floyd County, authorizing his or her entry or that of his or her representatives for the purpose of conducting the inspection or investigation. The term "emergency condition," for the purposes of this section, shall mean any condition or circumstance which the fire marshal or the fire chief determines to constitute an immediate threat or danger to the occupants of the building, structure, facilities or premises or to persons or property exposed to a fire out of control, the hazards associated with fire out of control, explosion, the threat of fire or explosion, or exposed to risks from some other hazardous condition or circumstances.
(c) Implied consent. Any application for, or the acceptance of, any approval, permit, license or certificate requested or required pursuant to this article, any applicable code or other applicable law or ordinance of the City of Rome or the state, constitutes agreement and consent by the person making the application, or accepting the approval, permit, license or certificate to allow the fire marshal or his or her representatives to enter the building, structure, facility or premises at any reasonable time to conduct inspections as may be deemed appropriate by the fire marshal or as otherwise provided by this article or other applicable state law or ordinance, or rules or regulations.
2-10-63.5 Notice of, or order to, eliminate dangerous or unlawful conditions.
(a) Notice of violations. Whenever the fire marshal or his or her designated representatives find any violations of this article, applicable adopted codes, or standards, or any fire hazards, as defined herein, they are authorized to issue or serve a written notice of the findings of an inspection as set forth in section 2-10-63.4 and to notify the building official. For the purposes of this article, a fire hazard means anything or act which increases or may cause an increase of the hazard or menace of fire out of control to a greater degree than that customarily recognized as normal by persons in the public service regularly engaged in preventing fires out of control; or which may obstruct, delay, hinder or interfere with the operations of the Rome-Floyd Fire Department or the egress of occupants in the event of fire out of control or other emergency condition, actual or perceived.
(b) Abatement order—Written. Whenever the fire marshal or his or her designated representatives find any violations of this article or any fire hazards, which are deemed to create a serious or significant potential for fire out of control or explosion or which are deemed to create a serious or significant potential threat to life in event of fire out of control or explosion, they are authorized to issue a written order to correct or abate the violations or hazards. Such order when issued shall set forth a reasonable and realistic time frame or date limit for correction, abatement or compliance. The time frame for correction, abatement or compliance established by or as directed by the fire marshal or his or her designated representative may be reasonably correlated by him or her or them to the seriousness or relative degree of hazard, and/or to the complexity of the means of correction or abatement.
(c) Abatement order—Verbal. Where deemed necessary, due to the potential risk to life or property, the fire marshal or his or her representative may issue a verbal order for the immediate correction or abatement of a violation or fire hazard. This may be followed by a written order of notice or action.
(d) Summary abatement. The fire marshal or the fire chief shall have the authority to summarily abate any violation of this article or any fire hazard, which constitutes an immediate or imminent danger or threat to life in their judgment, and where the following of the provisions for obtaining corrective action or abatement as set forth elsewhere in this article is not practical in their judgment.
(e) Unsafe buildings or structures. Any building or structure which is deemed to be structurally unsafe or which is not provided with adequate means of egress, or which is deemed to constitute a serious fire hazard, or which is otherwise deemed dangerous to human life, or which in relation to existing use constitutes a hazard to the safety, health or welfare to the public by reason of inadequate maintenance, dilapidation, obsolescence, fire damage, disaster damage, vandalism, flood damage or abandonment, as specified in this article or by any other applicable codes or ordinances in force in Floyd County, is deemed to be an unsafe building or structure.
2-10-63.6 Serving notices or orders.
(a) Generally. The service of notices or orders issued in connection with [subsections] 2-10-63.5(a) and 2-10-63.5(b) of this article may be made by the fire marshal or his or her representatives upon the owner, occupant or person in charge of the building, structure, facility, premises or portion thereof where the hazards or violations were found, or by delivering a copy of the notice or order to any or all of the persons noted. If such person(s) cannot be served by delivery as noted, service may be accomplished by affixing a copy of the notice or order in a conspicuous place at or near the entrance of the building, structure, facility or premises, or by delivering or sending a copy of the notice or order to the known agent of the owner or occupant, or in the event of an absentee owner with no known agent, by sending a copy by certified or registered mail to the owner's last known residence, business or post office address.
(b) To occupants of certain premises. If the building, structure, facility or premises is owned by one (1) or more persons and is occupied by one (1) or more other persons under lease or otherwise, the notice or order issued in connection with this section shall apply to the occupants thereof, except where the notice or order requires the addition to or changes in the building, structure or premises such as would immediately become real estate and become the property of the owners and not the occupants unless it is otherwise agreed between or among the owners and the occupants.
2-10-63.7 Penalty provisions.
(a) General penalty; separate violations. Any person who shall fail to comply with an order of correction or abatement as set forth in this section, or who shall build or act in violation of this article or of any detailed statement of specifications or plans submitted and approved under authority of this article in connection with any approval, certificate, or permit issued thereunder, or who shall perform any act deemed to create a serious potential for fire out of control, or explosion and for which the issuance of an order to correct or abate is not adequate, and who is found guilty shall be guilty of a violation of this article. A person found guilty under this section shall, for each violation and noncompliance, respectively, be subject to punishment by a fine of not less than one hundred dollars ($100.00), nor more than five thousand dollars ($5,000.00), or by imprisonment for a period of not more than one hundred twenty (120) days or by both such fine and imprisonment. The imposition of a penalty for any violation shall not excuse the violation or permit it to continue, and the responsible persons shall correct or abate such violation within a time limit as ordered by the court. When not otherwise specified, each five (5) days a prohibited condition or violation continues following an order of the court to correct or abate the same shall constitute a separate offense.
(b) Procedures upon determination of violation—Generally. When the fire marshal, the fire chief or their authorized representatives determine that violations of this Code warrant the filing of charges or action of the court as provided for in [subsection] 2-10-63.7(a), the issuing of a citation of charges and/or summons to appear before the Magistrate Court of Floyd County shall be served by any certified law enforcement officer of Floyd County upon request of the fire marshal, the fire chief or their authorized representative.
(c) Same—Injunctive relief. In addition to the filing of charges as specified in [subsections] 2-10-63.7(a) and 2-10-63.7(b), or as a separate remedy at law, the fire marshal or the fire chief may seek injunctive relief for any fire hazard, violation, or condition that threatens the safety of life or property based on the provisions of this Code or any applicable code or ordinance of Floyd County or of the State of Georgia.
(d) Removal of prohibited conditions. The application of penalties by the court as provided for in [section] 2-10-63.7 shall not be held to prevent the enforced removal of prohibited conditions or violations.
(e) Whenever in this Code any act is prohibited or is made or declared to be unlawful or an offense, or whenever in such Code the doing of any act is required or the failure to do any act is declared to be unlawful, where no specific penalty is provided therefor, the violation of any such provision of this Code shall be punished as authorized by section 2-1-8 of the Code of Ordinances of Floyd County, Georgia.
2-10-63.8 Removal of notices or order; illegal use of buildings.
(a) Removal, generally. It shall be unlawful for any person to remove any notice or order issued in connection with this article and affixed to a building, structure, facility, or premises, without the approval of the fire marshal or his or her authorized representative.
(b) Unlawful use of building or facility. It shall be unlawful for any person to use a building, structure, facility, or premises in violation of the provisions of this article where an order has been affixed to same prohibiting the use of same under authority of any provisions of this article without the approval of the fire marshal or his or her authorized representative or the court.
(c) Change of occupancy or use of building. When it is determined that the occupancy or use of a building has changed from that shown on the certificate of occupancy issued by the building official, the fire marshal, or the state fire marshal, the fire marshal may issue such notice or orders as necessary and in conformance with this article to remove or remedy any noted violations or hazards, and he or she shall refer the building to the building official, or as appropriate, the state fire marshal, for any repairs, alterations, remodeling, removing or demolition required.
2-10-63.9 Coordination with and application of related codes and standards.
(a) Changes in existing buildings or facilities. Any alterations, additions or changes required in existing buildings, structures, facilities, or premises because of a change in use, occupancy, exit design or other reason shall be made in compliance with the codes and standards adopted under this article and as set for in section 2-10-1 and 2-10-64 of this chapter.
(b) Review of plans coordinated. The fire marshal and the building official shall coordinate their review of plans on new construction and/or renovations or alterations of existing buildings or structures so as to ascertain compliance with this article and the codes and standards adopted by this article under their respective jurisdictions. The building official, pursuant to state, shall not issue any building permit on buildings under the jurisdiction of the state fire marshal (O.C.G.A. §§ 25-2-13 and 25-2-14), until the required state construction permit is issued by the state fire marshal.
(c) New construction. The fire marshal and the building official shall have the authority to jointly consider and approve a modification of any of the applicable codes for new construction with regard to matters relating to fire protection and safety to life in the event of fire out of control or related emergencies where the proposed designed, fire protection system, building use, or construction method involved is unusual or where it involves an unusual hazard, condition, or hardship, and the provisions of the codes and standards in force do not clearly or adequately deal with the proposed design, protection system application or design, building use, or construction method, in their judgment. Such approvals shall not result in a condition(s) that is/are less protective than any code or standard adopted by the state.
(d) Alternate materials. It is the intent of this provision to allow the use of designs, systems, methods, or devices of equivalent or superior quality, strength, fire resistance, effectiveness, durability, and safety to those prescribed by the applicable codes and standards, provided that technical documentation, data, or other information or material acceptable to the fire marshal and building official is submitted for review and such demonstrates to their satisfaction the equivalency of the design, system, method, or device for the intended use. Any modification or alternate safeguard jointly approved by the fire marshal and the building official shall not afford a condition less safe to life, and where appropriate, property, than in their judgment would be provided with compliance with the provisions of applicable codes or standards.
2-10-63.10 Modifications and appeals.
(a) Existing conditions. The fire marshal shall have the authority to modify any of the provisions of the adopted codes or standards adopted by reference by this article, except regarding buildings under the jurisdiction of O.C.G.A. § 25-2-13, upon application in writing by the owners and/or occupants of an existing building, structure, facility or premises, or by their authorized agents, when there are practical difficulties in the way of carrying out the strict letter of this Code or the codes or standards adopted by reference by this article or Floyd County. Such modification may be granted by the fire marshal, provided that in his judgment, the spirit, intents, and purposes of this article are observed, the public safety shall be reasonably and practically secured, the modification is in the interest of the community and substantial justice will be done. The particulars of any modification granted or allowed, and the decision of the fire marshal thereon, shall be entered upon the records of the division.
(b) Right to appeal. Whenever the fire marshal or the fire chief shall issue an order pursuant to this article, disapprove an application, refuse to grant a permit, refuse to grant a waiver or modification, or when it is claimed that the provisions of this article or the codes and standards adopted by reference by this article or Floyd County do not apply or that the true intent and meaning of same have been misconstrued or wrongly interpreted, the applicant or aggrieved person may appeal from the order or decision of the fire marshal or the fire chief to the board of adjustments as established by the adopted building code of Floyd County within thirty (30) days after the decision is rendered by the fire marshal or the fire chief. The provisions of the applicable building code relative to time limits, variations and modifications, and decisions as connected with the appeals to the board of adjustments shall be applicable to appeals from the fire marshal or the fire chief relating to this article. If the applicant or aggrieved person is not satisfied with the decision of the board of adjustments, appeal may be made to the court of appropriate jurisdiction. Every decision of the board of adjustments relative to this article shall be filed in the office of the fire marshal.
2-10-63.11 General provisions.
(a) Interference with fire officials. It shall be unlawful for any person to interfere with, abuse, or obstruct in any way the fire chief, the fire marshal, or their representatives in carrying out any actions in accordance with their official duties as set forth by this article, or by any other applicable local ordinance, or by any law or regulation of the State of Georgia.
(b) Unlawful use of credentials; unlawful impersonation of fire official. It shall be unlawful for any unauthorized person to use an official or unofficial badge or credential so as to impersonate an authorized fire official or to otherwise impersonate a fire official.
(c) Authority to investigate fires, explosions, false alarms or related incidents. The fire chief, the fire marshal or his authorized representatives are authorized to investigate the cause, origin and circumstances of any fire or explosion, or to investigate any incident resulting from the sending or sounding of a false alarm of fire or a bomb threat. When, in the judgment of the fire marshal, reasonable cause exists that a fire or explosion may have been of criminal origin, the fire marshal or his or her authorized representative is authorized to locate and take custody of any and all physical evidence relating to the cause of the fire or explosion and to continue the investigation to the extent deemed appropriate within the limits of division resources and within the limits of applicable state laws. The fire marshal shall inform the Floyd County Police Department of each fire of criminal or suspected criminal origin, false alarms, or bomb threats. The fire marshal shall also assist the Floyd County Police Department in its investigations of reported incidents, if so, requested by that department. The Floyd County Police Department shall be responsible for the investigation of fires and/or explosions of criminal or suspected criminal origin, false alarms or bomb threats so as to identify, apprehend and assist in the prosecution of the persons responsible for such criminal acts.
(d) Evacuation of buildings, structures, facilities or premises. When, in the judgment of the fire chief, the fire marshal, or their authorized representatives in their absence, there is an actual or serious potential danger to the occupants of or persons in close proximity to any building, structure, facility or premises because of unsafe structural conditions, or the presence of explosives, explosive fumes or vapor, toxic fumes, gases or materials, the fire chief, the fire marshal, or their authorized representatives in their absence, may order the complete or partial immediate evacuation of any building, structure, facility or premises and, as necessary, areas in such proximity to these as to be endangered. All persons under order to evacuate shall promptly leave the evacuation area and shall not reenter until authorized to do so by the official who issued the evacuation order. This section shall not pertain to bomb threats where no bomb or explosive device is known to exist. In such bomb threat situations, the decision to evacuate or not to evacuate is the responsibility of the person in charge of the building, structure, facility or premises at that time.
(e) Permits and approvals. A person shall not maintain, store, or handle materials, or conduct processes which produce conditions hazardous to life or property, or install equipment used in connection with such activities without first obtaining approval, or as appropriate based on the provisions of section 2-10-63.12 of this article, a permit from the fire marshal. Where conditions or activities are also regulated by a state or federal agency and a permit, license or certificate is required by the regulating agency, then no local permit is required; provided, however, the approval of the fire marshal is required, and he/she shall have the authority to apply the provisions of this article where a hazardous condition is discovered.
(f) Tests. All equipment required by this article or other applicable codes adopted by Floyd County or by the State of Georgia shall be maintained in a safe, sound, and operational condition. The fire marshal may require tests or test reports as proof of compliance. Required tests and reports are to be made at the expense of the owner or his agent by an approved testing laboratory or other approval agency or firm acceptable to the fire marshal.
(g) Authority to expose or stop work. Whenever any construction or installation coming under this article is subject to inspection prior to use and is covered or concealed without having first been inspected, the fire marshal may require by verbal and/or written order that such work be exposed for inspection. The fire marshal shall be notified when the installation is ready for inspection within a reasonable period. When any construction or installation work is being performed in violation of the plans, specifications or understandings as approved by the fire marshal, a written order may be issued to the responsible person to stop work on that portion of the work which is in violation. The order shall state the nature of the violation. No work shall be continued on that portion until the violation has been corrected and the order is lifted by the fire marshal or his or her designated representative.
(h) Effect of court decision. If, for any reason, any provision, section, subsection, clause or phrase of this article, or any code or standard adopted by reference by this article, is held to be invalid or unconstitutional by a decision of a court of competent jurisdiction, such decision shall not affect the validity of the remaining provisions of this article, or of any code or standard adopted by reference by this article.
2-10-63.12 Approvals and fire regulatory permits; related provisions.
(a) Fire regulatory permit and fire department services fee. The fire chief, fire marshal or their authorized representatives shall enforce the provisions of the fire regulatory permit and fire department services fees. These fees are in the Fee Schedule Book of Floyd County and adopted by the Floyd County Commission.
(b) For purposes of this Code, the word "permit" as used in the International Fire Code (IFC), shall be construed as being a "fire regulatory permit" as required under section 2-10-63.12 of the Fire Prevention Code. The fire regulatory permit fees shall be separate from the application process fee required by subsection 2-10-63.12(a). The permit application and issuance process established by section 2-10-63.12 shall apply.

(a) Findings; public purpose.
(1) Based on the experience of other urban counties, including, but not limited to Fulton County, DeKalb County, Richmond County, and Palm Beach, Florida, which experiences we believe are relevant to the problems faced by Floyd County, Georgia, the Floyd County Board of Commissioners takes note of the notorious and self-evident conditions attendant to the commercial exploitation of human sexuality, which do not vary greatly among generally comparable communities within our country. Further, the county board of commissioners finds that adult entertainment establishments, if unregulated, will likely lead to an increase in prostitution, venereal disease, drug and alcohol offenses and other criminal activity. Further, the board of commissioners finds that adult entertainment establishments sometimes are fronts for or operated by persons associated with organized criminal activities, and the need to scrutinize such dance establishments are thereby enhanced. Further, it is the finding of the board of commissioners that public nudity, either partial or total, under certain circumstances, particularly circumstances related to the sale and consumption of alcoholic beverages and/or beer begets criminal behavior and tends to create undesirable community conditions. The county board of commissioners further finds that there are certain undesirable community conditions that identify with nudity and alcohol, and they are the depression of property values in the surrounding neighborhood, the increased expenditures for and allocation of law enforcement personnel to preserve law and order, and the increased burden on the judicial system as a consequence of the criminal behavior hereinabove described. Further, the location of an adult entertainment establishment may, and most probably will, attract an undesirable quantity and quality of transients which adversely affect property values, causes an increase in crime and encourages residents and businesses therein to move elsewhere.
(2) Therefore, the limitation of nude conduct in establishments licensed to sell alcohol, beer and/or wine and/or establishments where there is consumption on the premises of alcohol, beer and/or wine is in the public welfare, and it is a matter of governmental interest and concern to prevent the occurrence of criminal behavior and undesirable community conditions normally associated with establishments which serve alcohol and also and/or encourage nudity. To that end, this ordinance [consisting of this section, 2-11-67] is hereby adopted.
(b) Enactment. The following types of entertainment, attire and conduct are prohibited upon any premises where beer, wine and/or alcoholic beverages are consumed on the premises:
(1) The employment or use of any person, in any capacity, in the sale or service of alcohol beverages while such person is unclothed or in such attire, costume or clothing, as to expose to view any portion of the female breast below the top of the areola or of any portion of the male or female pubic hair, anus, cleft of the buttocks, vulva and genitals.
(2) Live entertainment where any person appears in the manner described in subsection (b)(1) of this section or where such persons (or person) perform(s) acts of or acts which simulate any of the following:
a. Sexual intercourse, masturbation, sodomy, bestiality, oral copulation, flagellation or any sexual act which is prohibited by law.
b. The touching, caressing or fondling of the breasts, buttocks, anus or genitals.
c. The displaying of the male or female pubic hair, anus, vulva or genitals.
(2) The holding, promotion, sponsoring or allowance of any contest, promotion, special night, event or any other activity where patrons of the licensed establishment are encouraged or allowed to engage in any of the conduct described in subsections (b)(1) and (2) above.
(4) All dancing shall occur on a platform intended for that purpose which is raised at least two (2) feet from the level of the floor, and no dancing shall occur closer than ten (10) feet to any patron.
(5) No dancer shall fondle or caress any patron, and no patron shall fondle or caress any dancer.
(6) No patron shall directly pay or give any gratuity to any dancer, and no dancer shall solicit any pay or gratuity from any patron.
(c) Severability. It is hereby declared to be the intention of the county board of commissioners that the sections, paragraphs, sentences, clauses and phrases of this enactment are severable, and if any phrase, clause, sentence, paragraph or section hereof shall be declared unconstitutional by the valid judgment or decree of any court of competent jurisdiction, such unconstitutionality shall not affect any of the remaining phrases, clauses, sentences, paragraphs and sections of this enactment, since the same would have been enacted by the Floyd County Board of Commissioners without the incorporation herein of any such unconstitutional phrase, clause, sentence, paragraph or section.
(d) Violation—penalty. Any person violating the provisions of this ordinance shall be guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by a fine not to exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) per violation or by imprisonment for a period not to exceed six (6) months, or by both such fine and imprisonment. In addition to such fine and/or imprisonment, or in lieu thereof, violation of this ordinance shall also be grounds for the governing authority to apply for and obtain a temporary and/or permanent restraining order against such violations.

Applicable codes means (a) any optional housing or abatement standard provided in Chapter 2 of Title 8 of the O.C.G.A. as adopted by ordinance or operation of law, or general nuisance law, relative to the safe use of real property; (b) any fire or life safety code as provided for in Chapter 2 of Title 25 of the O.C.G.A.; and (c) any building codes adopted by local ordinance prior to October 1, 1991, or the minimum standard codes provided in O.C.G.A. Chapter 2 of Title 8 after October 1 provided that such building or minimum standard codes for real property improvements shall be deemed to mean those building or minimum standard codes in existence at the time such real property improvements were constructed unless otherwise provided by law.
Closing means causing a dwelling, building, or structure to be vacated and secured against unauthorized entry.
County means Floyd County, Georgia.
Drug crime means an act which is a violation of O.C.G.A. Article 2 of Chapter 13 of Title 16, known as the Georgia Controlled Substances Act.
Dwellings, buildings, or structures means any building or structure or part thereof used and occupied for human habitation or commercial, industrial, or business uses, or intended to be so used, and includes any outhouses, improvements, and appurtenances belonging thereto or usually enjoyed therewith and also includes any building or structure of any design. The term "dwellings, buildings, or structures" shall not be mean or include any farm, any building or structure located on a farm, or any agricultural facility or other building or structure used for the production, growing, raising, harvesting, storage, or processing of crops, livestock, poultry, or other farm products.
Governing authority means the Floyd County Commission.
Interested party means:
(1) Owner;
(2) Those parties having an interest in the property as revealed by a certification of title to the property conducted in accordance with the title standards of the State Bar of Georgia;
(3) Those parties having filed a notice in accordance with [O.C.G.A.] Code section 48-3-9;
(4) Any other party having an interest in the property whose identity and address are reasonably ascertainable from the records of the petitioner or records maintained in the county courthouse or by the clerk of the court. "Interested party" shall not include the holder of the benefit or burden of any easement or right of way whose interest is properly recorded which interest shall remain unaffected; and
(5) Persons in possession of said property and premises.
Owner means the holder of the title in fee simple and every mortgagee of record.
Public authority means any member of a governing authority, any housing authority officer, or any officer who is in charge of any department or branch of the government of the municipality, county, or state relating to health, fire, or building regulations or to other activities concerning dwellings, buildings; or structures in the county or municipality.
Public officer means the officer or officers who are authorized by O.C.G.A. section 41-2-7, section 41-2-8 and sections 41-2-9 through 41-2-17 and by this article adopted under section 41-2-7, section 41-2-8, and sections 41-2-9 through 41-2-17 to exercise the powers prescribed by this article or any agent of such officer or officers.
Repair means altering or improving a dwelling, building, or structure so as to bring the structure into compliance with the applicable codes in the jurisdiction where the property is located.
Resident means any person residing in the jurisdiction where the property is located on or after the date on which the alleged nuisance arose.
(Ord. No. 2005-003A, § 6, 10-25-05)
651:
(a) It is the duty of the owner of every dwelling, building, structure, or property within the jurisdiction to construct and maintain such dwelling, building, structure, or property in conformance with applicable codes in force within the county, or such ordinances which regulate and prohibit activities on property and which declare it to be a public nuisance to construct or maintain any dwelling, building, structure or property in violation of such codes or ordinances. It shall be unlawful for such owner to allow a dwelling, building, structure, or property within the jurisdiction to become unsafe, unsanitary, dangerous or detrimental to the health, safety, or welfare, or otherwise inimical to the welfare of the residents of the county or otherwise become a nuisance as set forth under this Code or the laws of this state.
(b) The County Commission of Floyd County, Georgia hereby appoints and designates the county code enforcement officer, county fire marshall, county police chief, and the Chief Building Inspector of the Rome/Floyd County Building Inspection Department and their respective designees as public officers to exercise the powers prescribed by this article.
(c) Whenever a request is filed with the public officer by a public authority or by at least two (2) residents of Floyd County, Georgia charging that any dwelling, building, or structure is unfit for human habitation or for commercial, industrial, or business use and not in compliance with applicable codes; is vacant and being used in connection with the commission of drug crimes; or constitutes an endangerment to the public health or safety as a result of unsanitary or unsafe conditions, the public officer shall make an investigation or inspection of the specific dwelling, building, structure, or property.
If the officer's investigation or inspection identifies that any dwelling, building, structure, or property is unfit for human habitation or for commercial, industrial, or business use and not in compliance, with applicable codes; is vacant and being used in connection with the commission of drug crimes; or constitutes an endangerment to the public health or safety as a result of unsanitary or unsafe conditions, the public officer may issue a complaint in rem against the lot, tract, or parcel of real property on which such dwelling, building, or structure is situated or where such public health hazard or general nuisance exists and shall cause summons and a copy of the complaint to be served on the interested parties for such dwelling, building, or structure.
The complaint shall identify the subject real property by appropriate street address and official tax map reference; identify the interested parties; state with particularity the factual basis for the action; and contain a statement of the action sought by the public officer to abate the alleged nuisance. The summons shall notify the interested parties that a hearing will be held before the Magistrate Court of Floyd County, at a date and time certain. Such hearing shall be held not less than fifteen (15) days nor more than forty-five (45) days after the filing of said complaint in court. The interested parties shall have the right to file an answer to the complaint and to appear in person or by attorney and offer testimony at the time and place fixed for the hearing.
The Magistrate Court of Floyd County shall have full jurisdiction to try and dispose of all such complaints.
(d) If after such notice and hearing, the court determines that the dwelling, building, or structure in question is unfit for human habitation or is unfit for its current commercial, industrial, or business use and not in compliance with applicable codes; is vacant and being used in connection with the commission of drug crimes; or constitutes an endangerment to the public health or safety as a result of unsanitary or unsafe conditions, the court shall state in writing findings of fact in support such determination and shall issue and cause to be served upon the interested parties that have answered the complaint or appeared at the hearing an order which:
(1) If the repair, alteration, or improvement of the said dwelling, building, or structure can be made at a reasonable cost in relation to the present value of the dwelling, building, or structure, requiring the owner, within the time specified in the order, to repair, alter, or improve such dwelling, building, or structure so as to bring it into full compliance with the applicable codes relevant to the cited violation and, if applicable, to secure the structure so that it cannot be used in connection with the commission of crimes; or
(2) If the repair, alteration, or improvement of the said dwelling, building, or structure in order to bring it into full compliance with applicable codes relevant to the cited violations cannot be made at a reasonable cost in relation to the present value of the dwelling, building, or structure, requiring the owner, within the time specified in the order, to demolish and remove such dwelling, building, or structure and all debris from the property.
For purposes of this article, the court shall make its determination of "reasonable cost in relation the present value of the dwelling, building or structure" without consideration of the value of the land on which the structure is situated; provided, however, that costs of the preparation necessary to repair, alter, or improve a structure may be considered. The income and financial status of the owner shall not be factor in the court's determination. The present value of the structure and the costs of repair, alteration, or improvement may be established by affidavits of real estate appraisers with a Georgia appraiser classification as provided in Chapter 39A of Title 41, of the O.C.G.A., qualified building contractors, or qualified building inspectors without actual testimony presented. Costs of repair, alteration, or improvement of the structure shall be the cost necessary to bring the structure into compliance with the applicable codes relevant to the cited violations in force in the jurisdiction.
(e) If the owner fails to comply with an order to repair or demolish the dwelling, building, or structure, the public officer may cause such dwelling, building, or structure, to be repaired, altered, improved, to be vacated and closed, or demolished. Such abatement action by the county shall commence within two hundred seventy (270) days after the expiration of time specified in the court order for abatement by the owner. Any time during which such action is prohibited by a court order issued pursuant to [O.C.G.A.] Code section 41-2-13 or any other equitable relief granted by a court of competent jurisdiction shall not be counted toward the two hundred seventy (270) days in which such abatement action must commence. The public officer shall cause to be posted on the main entrance of the building, dwelling, or structure a placed with the following words:
"This building is unfit for human habitation or commercial, industrial, or business use and does not comply with the applicable codes or has been ordered secured to prevent its use in connection with drug crimes or constitutes and endangerment to the public health or safety as a result of unsanitary or unsafe conditions. The use or occupation of this building is prohibited and unlawful."
(f) If the public officer has the structure demolished, reasonable effort shall be made to salvage reusable materials for credit against the cost of demolition. The proceeds of any moneys received from the sale of salvaged materials shall be used or applied against the cost of the demolition and removal of the structure, and proper records shall be kept showing application of sales proceeds. Any such sale of salvaged materials may be made without the necessity of public advertisement and bid. The public officer and the county are relieved of any and all liability resulting from or occasioned by the sale of any such salvaged materials, including, without limitation, defects in such salvaged materials.
(g) The public officers designated herein may issue citations for violations of state minimum standard codes, optional building, fire, life safety, and other codes adopted by ordinance, and conditions creating a public health hazard or general nuisance, and may seek to enforce such citation in any court of competent jurisdiction prior to issuing a complaint in rem as provided in this article.
(h) In addition to any other power or authority granted in this article to the court, the court shall have full jurisdiction and authority to punish persons found to have created, allowed or maintained a nuisance or other dangerous, unsafe or unsanitary condition and who have refused to abate the same, as provided for in the section 2-11-6 of the Floyd County Code.
(i) Nothing in this article shall be construed to impair or limit in any way the power of the county to define and declare nuisances and to summarily and without notice order the abatement of or abate any nuisance or dangerous condition where the case is an urgent one and the health and safety of the public or a portion thereof is in imminent danger.
(Ord. No. 2005-003A, § 7, 10-25-05)
654:
(a) Complaints issued by a public officer pursuant to this article shall be served in the following manner. At least fourteen (14) days prior to the date of the hearing, the public officer shall mail copies of the complaint by certified mail or statutory overnight delivery, return receipt requested, to all interested parties whose identity and address are reasonably ascertainable. Copies of the complaint shall also be mailed by first-class mail to the property address to the attention of the occupants of the property, if any, and shall be posted on the property within three (3) business days of filing the complaint and at least fourteen (14) days prior to the date of the hearing.
(b) For interested parties whose mailing address is unknown, a notice stating the date, time, and place of the hearing shall be published in the newspaper in which the sheriff's advertisements appear in such county once a week for two consecutive weeks prior to the hearing.
(c) Orders and other filings made subsequent to service of the initial complaint shall be served in the manner provided in this Code section on any interested party who answers the complaint or appears at the hearing. (Ord. No. 2005-003A, § 10, 10-25-05)
655:
(a) A notice of lis pendens shall be filed in the office of the Clerk of Superior Court of Floyd County at the time of filing the complaint in the Floyd County Magistrate Court. Such notice shall have the same force and effect as other lis pendens notices provided by law.
(b) The amount of the cost of demolition, including all court costs, appraisal fees, administrative costs incurred by the county tax commissioner or county revenue officer, and all other costs necessarily associated with the abatement action, including restoration to grade of the real property after demolition, shall be a lien against the real property upon which such cost was incurred.
(c) The lien provided for in this code section shall attach to the real property upon the filing of a certified copy of the order requiring repair, closure or demolition in the office of the Clerk of Superior Court of Floyd County and shall relate back to the date of the filing of the lis pendens notice required under subsection (c) of O.C.G.A. § 41-2-12. The clerk of superior court shall record and index such certified copy of the order in the deed records of Floyd County and enter the lien on the general execution docket. The lien shall be superior to all other liens on the property, except liens for taxes to which the lien shall be inferior, and shall continue in force until paid.
(d) Upon final determination of costs, fees, and expenses incurred in accordance with this chapter, the public officer responsible for enforcement actions in accordance with this Code section shall transmit to the county tax commissioner or county revenue officer a statement of the total amount due and secured by said lien, together with copies of all notices provided to interested parties. The statement of the public officer shall be transmitted within ninety (90) days of completion of the repairs, demolition, or closure. It shall be the duty of the appropriate county tax commissioner or county revenue officer, who is responsible or whose duties include the collection of county taxes, to collect the amount of the lien using all methods available for collecting real property ad valorem taxes, including specifically [O.C.G.A.] Chapter 4 of Title 48; provided, however, that the limitation of [O.C.G.A.] Code Section 48-4-78 which requires twelve (12) months of delinquency before commencing a tax foreclosure shall not apply. A county tax commissioner shall collect and enforce county liens imposed pursuant to this chapter in accordance with [O.C.G.A.] Code Section 48-5-359.1. The county tax commissioner or county revenue officer shall remit the amount collected to Floyd County, Georgia.
(e) Enforcement of liens pursuant to this Code section may be initiated at any time following receipt by the county tax commissioner or county revenue officer of the final determination of costs in accordance with this Code section. The unpaid lien amount shall bear interest and penalties from and after the date of final determination of costs in the same amount as applicable to interest and penalties on unpaid real property ad valorem taxes. An enforcement proceeding pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-4-78 for delinquent ad valorem taxes may include all amounts due under this chapter.
(f) The redemption amount in any enforcement proceeding pursuant to this Code section shall be the full amount of the costs as finally determined in accordance with this Code section together with interest, penalties, and costs incurred by the governing authority, county tax commissioner, or county revenue officer in the enforcement of such lien. Redemption of property from the lien may be made in accordance with the provisions of O.C.G.A. §§ 48-4-80 and 48-4-81.
(g) The county may waive and release any such lien imposed on property upon the owner of such property entering into a contract with the county agreeing to a timetable for rehabilitation of the real property of the dwelling, building, or structure on the property and demonstrating the financial means to accomplish such rehabilitation.
(h) Any person affected by an order requiring the abatement of a nuisance, including the closure, repair, alteration, improvement, or demolition of a dwelling, building, or structure issued by the Floyd County Magistrate Court may petition the Superior Court of Floyd County by direct appeal under O.C.G.A. § 5-3-29.
(Ord. No. 2005-003A, § 11, 10-25-05; Ord. No. 2008-003A, § I, 5-27-08)
656:
In addition to having a dwelling, building, or structure closed pursuant to an order under Code section 2-11-84, a public officer may bring an immediate, emergency action ordering the closing of a dwelling, building, or structure in urgent cases where such property is found to be unfit for human habitation or for commercial, industrial, or business uses. Such emergency petition may be brought prior to issuing a complaint for the abatement of a nuisance under this article.
A petition requesting an emergency closing may be brought under the following conditions:
(a) After inspection of a dwelling, building, or structure, a public officer may proceed with filing an emergency petition to close the property upon finding that the dwelling, building, or structure constitutes an immediate danger to the health, safety and welfare of those persons visiting, working or residing within such dwelling, building, or structure, and that imminent harm to the occupants thereof has occurred or is likely to result from the continued use of such dwelling, building, or structure.
(b) The public officer shall prepare a petition which shall identify subject real property by appropriate street address and official tax map reference; identify the owner and known residents or users of the subject property; identify the exact nature of danger and all applicable codes relevant to such danger. The complaint shall also contain a statement requesting the closure of the dwelling, building, or structure.
(c) A hearing shall be scheduled by the magistrate court as soon as practicable, given the nature of the danger and the likelihood of injury alleged in the complaint.
(d) The owner of the property and any person in possession of said property and premises shall be served personally with a copy of the complaint whenever possible. The public officer, any officer of the Floyd County Police Department, and any person authorized by the State of Georgia as a process server may attempt to make such personal service. Failure to perfect personal service shall not be cause to dismiss the complaint or postpone the hearing. Where personal service is not obtained on all of the above parties, a copy of the complaint shall be posted on the property on the date the complaint is filed. In addition, the public officer shall mail copies of the complaint by certified mail or statutory overnight delivery, return receipt requested, and by first-class mail, to the residents and owner of the property. In the case of single-family dwellings, service on one (1) adult (persons eighteen (18) years of age and over) resident of the property shall be sufficient to obtain personal service. In the case of multi-family dwellings, service must be attempted for each residential unit.
(e) If after such notice and hearing, the magistrate court determines that the dwelling, building, or structure in question is unfit for human habitation or is unfit for its current commercial, industrial, or business use, is not in compliance with applicable codes, and constitutes an immediate danger to the health, safety and welfare of those persons working or residing within such dwelling, building, or structure, the court shall state in writing findings of fact in support of such determination and shall issue and cause to be served upon the owner and residents an order to close such dwelling, building, or structure. The court may place such conditions as are reasonable on the opening of such property, including the repair of the dwelling, building, or structure.
(f) Notwithstanding the foregoing, in cases where the conditions of a dwelling, building, or structure are so dangerous that a delay in closing such dwelling, building, or structure would/could cause a substantial likelihood of immediate harm or injury to those persons visiting, working or residing therein, the chief building official, Floyd County Police Chief or his designee or the county manager may issue an order temporarily closing the property pending a hearing in magistrate court. In that event, the public officer shall proceed with filing a petition and scheduling a hearing using the provisions set forth under this Code section. Any hearing held under this paragraph (f) shall be scheduled no later than seventy-two (72) hours after the temporary closing of the property.
(g) All orders by the magistrate court to close the property and all temporary orders by the chief building official, Floyd County Chief of Police or his designee or the county manager to temporarily close a property shall be binding on all persons, and failure to abide by such orders shall be a violation of this Code and is enforceable by the Floyd County Police Department or any authorized law enforcement agency. The chief building official, Floyd County Police Chief or his designee or the county manager may, in his discretion, allow persons to temporarily enter onto a closed dwelling, building, or structure for the purpose of removing personal property or to secure the dwelling, building, or structure.
(Ord. No. 2008-003A, § I, 5-27-08)
657:
(a) Definitions. The following words, terms, and phrases, when used in this section, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this subsection, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Camp or camping shall mean the use of an area for living-accommodation purposes such as sleeping activities or making preparations to sleep (including the laying down of bedding for the purpose of sleeping), or storing personal property or storing other belongings, making a fire, carrying on cooking activities, or using a tent, or other structure for habitation. These activities constitute camping if, in light of all the circumstances, it reasonably appears that in conducting one (1) or more of these activities, the person is in fact using the area as a living accommodation, regardless of the intent of the person or the nature of any other activities in which the person may also be engaging.
Interference with ingress or egress shall mean camping, storing personal property, standing, sitting, lying down, using personal property, or performing any other activity where such activity:
(1) Materially interferes with the ingress into or egress from buildings, driveways, streets, alleys, or any other real property that has a limited number of entrances or exits, regardless of whether the property is owned in whole or in part by Floyd County, a private owner, or another public entity, unless having received the prior express written permission of the property owner; or
(2) Reasonably appears, in light of all of the circumstances, to have the purpose or effect of blocking ingress into or egress from buildings, driveways, streets, alleys, or any other real property that has a limited number of entrances or exits, regardless of whether the property is owned in whole or in part by Floyd County, a private owner, or another public entity, unless having received the prior express written permission of the property owner.
Public area shall mean an area to which the public or a substantial group of persons has access, including, but not limited to, streets, highways, roadways (including shoulders and medians), bridges, the area above and below any bridge, sidewalks, alleys, parking lots and decks, plazas, parks, public greenspace areas, playgrounds, schools, transportation facilities, within a public-transportation vehicle, an area owned in whole or in part by, operated by, for, or under the custody and control of Floyd County, Georgia, and other public property, including county-owned property and any other property where public gatherings occur on a regular basis, and any other property where public meetings are conducted.
Storing personal property shall mean leaving one's personal effects, including, but not limited to, clothing, bedrolls, cookware, sleeping bags, luggage, knapsacks, backpacks, wagons, or shopping carts, unattended for more than one (1) hour. This term shall not include the parking of a bicycle in an approved bicycle stand or designated parking area.
(b) Prohibited acts. Unless the location is a designated campground or camping is otherwise authorized by Floyd County, it shall be unlawful for any person within Floyd County, Georgia to commit any of the following acts:
(1) No person shall camp in a public area.
(2) No person shall interfere with ingress or egress of any public area, or any building or private property without the demonstrable consent of the building or private property owner.
(c) Non-prohibited acts. Nothing in this section shall prohibit authorized county employees/agencies authorizing activities in the performance of their official duties.
(d) Warning for first offense. No person may be issued a citation or arrested for violating this section until that person has received a verbal or written warning to cease the unlawful conduct. If the person fails to promptly comply with the warning issued, then that person may be issued a citation or arrested.
(e) Other remedies for prohibited acts. Notwithstanding the issuance of a citation or arrest of a person violating this section, any personal property used to camp, in which a citation was issued, or being stored, as defined above, may be deemed abandoned by Floyd County, Floyd County Sheriff, or Floyd County Police Department and may be confiscated by them without prior warning. Floyd County, Floyd County Sheriff or Floyd County Police Department shall retain the property in a manner consistent with the handling of other confiscated or abandoned property.
(Ord. No. 05, 2024, 9-24-24)

660:
The intent of the Floyd County Board of Commissioners in enacting this article is to enable the county to promote the safety of citizens and to maintain all county roads and rights-of-way in a proper and safe operating condition and to provide a permit process concerning timber harvesting in Floyd County. The ordinance codified in this article is meant to be in compliance with O.C.G.A. § 12-6-24 of the State of Georgia Code of Ordinances. If any portion of the ordinance is in derogation of the above code section, the state law will prevail.
(Ord. of 5-9-17(2))
661:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
County road means any county owned or maintained highway, road, street, avenue, drive, detour or other way open to the public and intended or used for the passage of motor vehicles.
Operations means those activities contemplated by this article, including the loading or transporting of raw materials such as stone, timber, oil and fill dirt.
Right-of-way means any area occupied by a roadway and the areas and facilities immediately adjacent to a roadway to include the shoulder, front slope, ditch, drain, back slope and any areas beyond such that have been acquired and/or accepted by the county for the purpose of maintaining such areas and facilities.
Timber harvester means any individual, partnership, corporation, association or private organization of any character and the officer's agents and employees thereof carrying out the activities contemplated by this article.
(Ord. of 5-9-17(2))
662:
(a) All persons or firms harvesting standing timber in any unincorporated area of Floyd County for delivery as pulpwood, logs, poles, posts, or wood chips to any woodyard or processing plant located inside or outside this state shall provide notice of such harvesting operations to the Floyd County Board of Commissioners or the designated agent thereof prior to entering onto the property if possible, but in no event later than twenty-four (24) hours after entering onto the property. Further, such persons shall give notice of cessation of cutting within twenty-four (24) hours after the job is completed.
(b) The notice of harvesting operations required by this article shall be provided for each separate tract to be harvested. Such notice shall be made in such form as prescribed by rule or regulation of the Director of the Georgia Forestry Commission, and shall include the following information:
(1) A map of the area which identifies the location of the tract to be harvested and, as to those trucks which will be traveling to and from such tract for purposes of picking up and hauling loads of cut forest products, the main point of ingress to such tract from a public road and, if different, the main point of egress from such tract to a public road. If multiple points of ingress and/or ingress will be used, all such points shall be identified;
(2) A statement as to whether the timber will be removed pursuant to a lump sum sale, per unit sale, or owner harvest for purposes of ad valorem taxation under O.C.G.A. § 48-5-7.5;
(3) The name, address, and daytime telephone number of the timber seller if the harvest is pursuant to a lump sum or per unit sale or of the timber owner if the harvest is an owner harvest; and
(4) The name, business address, business telephone number, and nighttime or emergency telephone number of the person or firm harvesting such timber.
(c) Subject to the provisions of § 2-11-113(e) of this article, the notice required by this article may be submitted in person, by transmission of an electronic record via telefacsimile or e-mail, or by mail.
(d) Subject to the provisions of § 2-11-113(e) of this article, upon notification published by the Director of the Georgia Forestry Commission that a state-wide notification website or platform is available for public use, persons or firms wishing to utilize said website or platform to provide the notice required by this article may do so at their option, and Floyd County will accept notifications submitted in this manner.
(e) On and after a date specified and published by the Director of the Georgia Forestry Commission, use of the state-wide notification website or platform shall be mandatory and shall be the sole means of providing the notice required by this article; on and after said date submission of the notice by any of the means listed in § 2-11-113(c) above shall cease and will no longer be deemed acceptable or in compliance with this article.
(Ord. of 5-9-17(2); Res. of 2-8-22, § 2)
663:
Any person or firm commercially harvesting timber within the unincorporated areas of Floyd County shall provide to the Floyd County Engineering Department proposed haul routes prior to harvesting any timber. The engineering department shall review and approve all haul routes as proposed or with changes specified by the department. Timber harvesters shall be required to follow the approved haul routes specified and approved by the department.
(Ord. of 5-9-17(2))
664:
(a) No person or firm commercially harvesting timber within the unincorporated areas of Floyd County shall allow dirt, mud or other debris resulting from timber operations to accumulate upon the right-of-way of any public road to such an extent that it becomes a nuisance or a hazard to persons traveling upon said roads or creates an unsightly condition upon the public right-of-way.
(b) No person or firm commercially harvesting timber within the unincorporated areas of Floyd County shall allow dirt, mud or other debris resulting from timber operations to accumulate in the ditches and drainage areas on public rights-of-way to such an extent that the usual flow of water or runoff is stopped, disturbed, changed or interrupted.
(c) No person or firm commercially harvesting timber within the unincorporated areas of Floyd County shall create any other type of public nuisance or hazard within the rights-of-way of the county.
(d) No person or firm commercially harvesting timber within the unincorporated areas of Floyd County shall park or leave unattended a truck or other motor vehicle or trailer upon any county maintained right-of-way for any period of time.
(e) All persons or firms commercially engaging in timber harvesting operations within the unincorporated areas of Floyd County shall implement and maintain at all times soil erosion and sedimentation control best management practices, as prescribed by the Georgia Forestry Commission, US EPA and the Georgia Soil and Water Conservation Commission sufficient to prevent dirt, mud and other debris from accumulating in the county drainage ditches and on the county roads upon which the timber harvester is ingressing and egressing.
(Ord. of 5-9-17(2))
665:
No person or firm commercially harvesting timber within the unincorporated areas of Floyd County shall commence timber operations until he has first posted or caused to be posted along the public road onto which the timber harvester will enter from his timber operations at least the following signs: One (1) sign in each direction located five hundred (500) feet from the entrance which states "Slow Trucks Entering Highway"; one (1) sign in each direction located one thousand (1,000) feet from the entrance stating "Warning: Logging Operation Ahead". Each such sign shall be thirty-six (36) inches by thirty-six (36) inches, orange in color and posted at least three (3) feet from the surface of the road.
(Ord. of 5-9-17(2))
666:
(a) The notice required by this ordinance shall not be or remain effective unless and until the person or firm providing such notice has delivered to the Board of Commissioners of Floyd County or its designated agent a valid surety bond, executed by a surety corporation authorized to transact business in this state, protecting Floyd County against any damage caused by such person or firm in the amount of five thousand dollars ($5,000.00); provided, however, that at the option of the person or firm harvesting timber a valid irrevocable letter of credit issued by a bank or savings and loan association, as defined in O.C.G.A. § 7-1-4, in the amount of five thousand dollars ($5,000.00) may be provided in lieu of a surety bond. Such bonds or letters of credit shall be subject to the conditions set forth in subsections 2-11-117(b) and (c) of this article. No more than one (1) bond or letter of credit shall be required from each person or firm harvesting timber, regardless of the number of tracts harvested in the county for so long as the bond or letter of credit remains in effect. The bond or letter of credit required herein shall be valid only for the calendar year in which it was delivered.
(b) The bond or letter of credit required by subsection 2-11-117(a) of this article shall protect Floyd County against any damage requiring re-ditching or repair of existing ditch structures or the removal of any harvesting residue, including tree tops, debris, logs, pulpwood and other materials, placed in or around the county's rights-of-way caused by such person or firm tendering the bond or letter of credit. The provisions of this article have neither the purpose nor effect of imposing a limitation or restriction on the content or reasonable access to any communicative materials, including sexually oriented materials.
